(a) response requirements added in fixed ratio to fixed interval have no effect on response rate when the fixed interval is short, but have a substantial effect on response rate at longer fixed intervals, (b) response rate is higher under fixed ratio than under fixed interval when the ratio is small and the fixed interval is relatively short, but is higher under fixed interval than under fixed ratio when the ratio is large or the fixed interval is long, (c) response rate under fixed ratio is higher than response rate

(a) the tandem schedule maintained responding better than the corresponding fixed-interval schedule when the tandem schedule's ratio requirement was small, and (b) the tandem schedule's ability to maintain responding decreased as its ratio requirement was increased and as the fixed interval was increased.
(1) the effect of tandem schedules on response strength is to enhance responding and (2) the net effect of tandem schedules depends on the length and the ratio requirement.

the effects of reinforcement frequency on the maintenance of responding.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of tandem schedules are determined by the interaction of response requirements, reinforcement frequency, and fixed-interval value.
the effects of tandem schedules depend on the interaction of response requirements, reinforcement frequency, and fixed-interval length.
the effect of response requirements in tandem schedules is to enhance responding at short fixed intervals and to reduce it at long fixed intervals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of response requirements added to a fixed-interval schedule on the maintenance of responding depend on the interaction of the response requirement with the fixed-interval value.
reinforcement frequency is the primary determinant of response strength and that response requirements have an effect only when they do not substantially alter the reinforcement frequency.
the effects of response requirements in tandem schedules depend on both response requirements and reinforcement frequencies, and that the latter are a function of fixed-interval length.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reinforcement frequency of tandem schedules is determined by the ratio requirement, and the reinforcement frequency of the fixed-interval schedules is determined by fixed-interval length.
the effects of tandem schedules on behavior depend on the relative effects of the tandem schedule on reinforcement frequency and response strength.
the reinforcement-theory account can explain the effects of tandem schedules on response strength in terms of reinforcement frequency.
